The Respondent will not make any claim in connection with a decision by the Principal to exercise or not to exercise any of its rights in relation to the Invitation Process.

The Respondent is responsible for making its own investigation and assessment about all matters relevant to the Request for Tender, the Requirements, the accuracy of all information and Documents provided by or on behalf of the Principal, and all other matters relevant to the Respondent’s Tender.
Participation in the Invitation Process is at the Respondent’s cost.

direct all enquiries relating to the Request for Tender to the Principal’s nominated contact person, and not discuss the Request for Tender with any other person except as required to prepare its Tender.
ensure that all information provided as part of its Tender is complete, accurate, current, and not misleading.
comply with all Laws.

keep confidential all confidential Information which it obtains as part of the Invitation Process, not use it except for the purpose of responding to the Request for Tender, and not disclose it except to its Personnel on a need to know basis for the purpose of responding to the Request for Tender, or with the Principal’s consent, or to the extent required by Law, or to its professional advisors.

if it collects or has access to any Personal Information in connection with the Invitation Process, comply as if it was the Principal with the privacy principles in the Privacy Act or the Australian Privacy Principles in the Privacy Act, as applicable, in relation to that Personal Information and comply with all reasonable directions of the Principal relating to the Personal Information;
not make any public announcements or advertisement relating to the Invitation Process.
ensure that its Personnel also comply with these requirements.

ensure that all representations, warranties, declarations, statements, information and Documents (“information”) made or provided by the Respondent in connection with the Invitation Process are complete, accurate, up-to-date and not misleading in any way.
The Respondent must immediately tell the Principal if any information is or becomes incomplete, inaccurate, out-of-date or misleading in any way.

The Respondent warrants that neither it, nor its Personnel have engaged in any collusive, anti-competitive or similar conduct in connection with the Invitation Process or any actual or potential Contract with any entity for goods and Services similar to the Goods and Services.

The Respondent warrants that it and its Personnel do not hold any office or possess any property, are not engaged in any business or activity and do not have any obligations whereby a Conflict of Interest is created, or may appear to be created, in conflict with its obligations under these Request for Tender Conditions or the proposed Contract, except as disclosed in the Respondent’s Tender.

The Respondent warrants that it will not, and it will ensure that its Personnel do not, place themselves in a position that may give rise to a Conflict of Interest between the interest of the Principal and the Respondent’s interests during the Invitation Process.
The Respondent warrants that it will immediately notify the Principal if any Conflict of Interest arises after lodgement of the Respondent’s Tender.

The Respondent warrants that it will immediately notify the Principal if it becomes aware that any warranty made in this section was inaccurate, incomplete, out-of-date or misleading in any way when made, or becomes inaccurate, incomplete, out-of-date or misleading in any way, during the relevant period.

Operating the Waste Transfer Station site in accordance with the Environmental Protection Act 1986 and to undertake any reasonable direction given by the Principal for the effective operation of the Waste Transfer Station site;
The opening and secure closing of the Waste Transfer Station site located on the Narembeen South Road, (2km east of the townsite) at designated times provided by the Principal.

Current opening times are 4 days per week - Tuesday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, with adopted opening hours of 10.00am to 4.00pm on the stated days, equating to 24 hours of weekly site management with an additional 1 hour per fortnight to inspect and clean outside the fence line, unless varied by direction of the Shire of Narembeen.
Providing access to authorised Shire of Narembeen personnel and approved waste delivery vehicles including Avon Waste and Wren Oil, to all waste disposal areas as required.
Providing access to and recording of volumes of waste oil delivery to the oil disposal tank and hardstand.
To take down the name and address of persons disposing of oil for invoicing purposes and providing this information to the Shire of Narembeen administration staff for invoicing.

Collection of all windblown refuse found outside the Waste Transfer Station site boundaries (off site), and returning back to the Waste Transfer Station on a regular basis or when requested to do so by the Principal due to a complaint being received or windblown litter being observed during inspection.
Remove and set down recyclables in the appropriate designated areas as determined by the Principal and the Tenderer.
Maintain safe and suitable public access to the designated areas for refuse, oil, green waste and recyclables drop off areas.
Alert the Principal of any activity which is or appears to be illegal or not conducive to the proper use of the Waste Transfer Station.
The Contractor is to allow access to the Drum Muster area by the nominated association.
The appointed Contractor is to provide labour for required services, vehicle and mobile phone and other equipment and/or tools for provision of the Contract at the Narembeen Waste Transfer Station.
Mobile communication is required for contact purposes with the Shire of Narembeen.
You are required to comply with the requirements of the Occupational Health & Safety Act whilst undertaking the required agreed Waste Site Contractor Services.
This includes wearing correct footwear and a visible safety vest whilst onsite at all times.
The Narembeen Waste Transfer Station site shall remain neat and tidy at all times including stockpiles of timber, green waste, plastics, glass, cans, steel, rubble, paper, electrical equipment, etc.
Day to day training will be the responsibility of the Contractor.
The Contractor will be responsible for day-to-day site inductions.

The Contractor is to act under direction of the Shire of Narembeen’s appointed representative/s at all times, that includes the appointed Environmental Health Officer, the Works Manager and/or ultimately report directly to the Chief Executive Officer.

Assist the Principal or the Principal’s representative to undertake compliance inspections for Contract compliance and/or compliance with the Environmental Protection Act 1986 and any other Statutory requirement imposed on the Principal with regard to Waste Transfer Station operations or directions by the governing State Government Department

The Contractor is required to adequately keep records, as required by the Shire of Narembeen including but not limited to: classes of waste being deposited at the site, recycle bin exchange with farmers, the type of user ie: town and/or farmer, Contractor, preferred days of opening, etc.

Burning at the Waste Transfer Station shall only be completed as identified and required by approval for the “left over” green waste that cannot be utilised for garden mulch and/or other household requirements.
Approval to burn must be obtained from the Shire of Narembeen prior.
No burning shall be undertaken during the Prohibited Burning Period or the Restricted Burning Period, unless approval has been obtained from the Shire of Narembeen stating reasons why.
Generally, requirement to burn shall be undertaken during the winter months and outside of the restricted and prohibited burning periods.
Requests for assistance with Shire of Narembeen machinery shall be made direct to the Works Manager.
The request shall be timely for the required works to be completed and shall not be made direct to any works staff member.

Provision of certified current insurance cover and related copies for the provision of Waste Transfer Station Operation and Management Services shall be provided to the Shire of Narembeen on an annual basis.

The Contractor shall use only vehicles to suit the day-to-day operations of the Waste Transfer Station site provided by the Principal or as authorised for use by the Principal if not a Shire of Narembeen vehicle.
All vehicles used by the Contractor shall: - a. Be maintained in a reliable mechanical condition;
Be licensed and compliant with applicable Acts, Regulations and Local Laws;
Be driven by competent, qualified and licensed operators either being the Contractor or the staff of the Contractor;
Be regularly maintained and serviced.
The Contractor is required to develop and maintain both a Risk Management Plan and a Safety Management Plan for the activities of the Waste Transfer Station Operation and Management Contract.
